However, careful verification shows that because Winding Constrictor's counter-doubling effect only depends on it being alive at the time of each trigger, the same total of 5 Archfiend triggers occurs, with the same first 4 being amplified and the 5th not, regardless of order. This produces an identical final result: Rishkar and Tireless Tracker die early, Winding Constrictor dies at the 4th trigger, and Verdurous Gearhulk dies at the 5th (unamplified) trigger. The mana costs are also fully feasible (7 total mana from 4 Islands and 3 Swamps, with correct color distribution enabling Brilliant Spectrum's Converge to draw 2 cards). Shadowstorm Vizier ends at 6/8, Archfiend of Ifnir stays 5/4, and Stromkirk Condemned becomes 3/3, totaling exactly 14 power against the opponent's 14 life with no blockers remaining. This is a valid, distinct, and correct alternate solution.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

4200:702.29. Cycling
4202:702.29a Cycling is an activated ability that functions only while the card with cycling is in a player’s hand. “Cycling [cost]” means “[Cost], Discard this card: Draw a card.”

content.thinking:
Yes, discard this, draw a card. So net, replace the card with a new one, and it's a discard.
I need to win this turn, so let's think about the best way to use my cyclers and discard effects to pump up my board and then finish the game.

First, I can cycle Floodwaters for {2} to draw a Swamp, and cycle Horror for {B} to draw another Swamp. That gives me 2 discards from cycling, plus I can discard Brilliant Spectrum (which costs {3}{U} and converges to draw X cards where X is the number of colors spent—here it's 2 colors so draws 2, then discards 2). I also have Stromkirk's once-per-turn discard ability.

To maximize triggers on Archfiend, I need to discard as many cards as possible without discarding Archfiend itself. Each discard triggers Archfiend for 2 -1/-1 counters on every opponent creature, and cycling also triggers it.

If I discard 5 times total, Gearhulk (9 toughness) will 10 -1/-1 and die, Constrictor (8) dies, Rishkar (4) dies, and Tracker (4) dies. That's all blockers gone.

I can do exactly that: cycle Floodwaters, cycle Horror, use Stromkirk to discard one card, and Brilliant Spectrum to discard two. 5 discards total, all triggering Archfiend.

But if I play Horror instead of cycling it, I get only 3 discards (cycle Floodwaters, Stromkirk, Spectrum), which is enough to kill the small creatures (Rishkar and Tracker) but leaves Constrictor and Gearhulk alive. 3 discards give -6 toughness, so Gearhulk has 3 left and Constrictor has 2 left.

I have 7 mana. I can cast Floodwaters ({4}{U}{U}) to bounce the two big blockers instead of cycling it, then use my remaining discards to kill the small 2. But I need to check mana sequencing.

Better plan: sacrifice Archfiend (MV 5) for Elder Deep-Fiend emerge, which reduces cost to {U}{U}. I cast Horror first ({4}{B}), tapping 3 Swamps (1 for B, 2 generic) and 2 Islands (2 generic), leaving exactly {U}{U} for Elder. Then cast Elder, tapping all 4 opponent creatures so they can't block.

Hand left: Brilliant Spectrum and Floodwaters. I activate Stromkirk to discard one (say Floodwaters), triggering Vizier (+1) and Horror (+2). Stromkirk 2/2 +1 from its ability becomes 3/2.

Damage: Vizier 2 flying, Horror 6, Stromkirk 3, Elder 5 = 16. All attacking, no blockers possible. Win.

But summoning sickness: Horror and Elder can't attack this turn. So I need to flash Elder after declaring attackers.

Declare attackers with my 3 existing creatures (Vizier, Archfiend, Stromkirk) first. Then cast Elder sacrificing one attacker, so that one doesn't deal damage, but the other two do. Still short on damage.

I need to pump more before combat. Let's cycle both cyclers 2 discards, Stromkirk discard 1, Spectrum discard 2 = 5 discards. All blockers die from Archfiend. My original creatures attack unblocked: Vizier +5 =6/8, Archfiend 5, Stromkirk +1 =3, total 14 exactly.

Mana: 1B (Horror cycle) + 2 (Floodwaters cycle) + 3U +1U (Spectrum) =7 mana, perfect with my lands.

Sequence: cycle Horror, cycle Floodwaters, Stromkirk discard (say Elder), cast Spectrum (draw 2 Swamps, discard 2). All 5 discards happen before combat. No new creatures, no sickness, all 3 attack for 14. Win.

Yes, that works. I don't need to play Horror or Elder at all. 5 discards kill everything, and my pumped attackers finish it.   <solution>

All blockers die. Attack with Vizier (+5 to 6 8 flying), Archfiend (5), Stromkirk (+1 to 3). 14 damage unblocked.

Some effects may increase or reduce the cost to pay, or may provide other alternative costs. Costs may include paying mana, tapping permanents, sacrificing permanents, discarding cards, and so on. The total cost is the mana cost or alternative cost (as determined in rule 601.2b), plus all additional costs and cost increases, and minus all cost reductions. If multiple cost reductions apply, the player may apply them in any order. If the mana component of the total cost is reduced to nothing by cost reduction effects, it is considered to be {0}. It can’t be reduced to less than {0}. Once the total cost is determined, any effects that directly affect the total cost are applied. Then the resulting total cost becomes “locked in.” If effects would change the total cost after this time, they have no effect.

2557:603.2. Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically triggers. The ability doesn’t do anything at this point.
2559:603.2a Because they aren’t cast or activated, triggered abilities can trigger even when it isn’t legal to cast spells and activate abilities. Effects that preclude abilities from being activated don’t affect them.
2561:603.2b When a phase or step begins, all abilities that trigger “at the beginning of” that phase or step trigger.
2563:603.2c An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs. However, it can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.
2566:603.2d An ability may state that a triggered ability triggers additional times. In this case, rather than simply determining that such an ability has triggered, determine how many times it should trigger, then that ability triggers that many times. An effect that states that an ability triggers additional times doesn’t invoke itself repeatedly and doesn’t apply to other effects that affect how many times an ability triggers. An effect that states a triggered ability of an object triggers additional times refers only to triggered abilities that object has, not to any delayed or reflexive triggered abilities (see rule 603.7 and rule 603.12) that may be created by abilities the object has.
2568:603.2e Some trigger events use the word “becomes” (for example, “becomes attached” or “becomes blocked”). These trigger only at the time the named event happens—they don’t trigger if that state already exists or retrigger if it persists. An ability that triggers when a permanent “becomes tapped” or “becomes untapped” doesn’t trigger if the permanent enters the battlefield in that state.
2571:603.2f If a triggered ability’s trigger condition is met, but the object with that triggered ability is at no time visible to all players, the ability does not trigger.
2573:603.2g An ability triggers only if its trigger event actually occurs. An event that’s prevented or replaced won’t trigger anything.
2576:603.2h A triggered ability may have an instruction followed by “Do this only once each turn.” This ability triggers only if its source’s controller has not yet taken the indicated action that turn.
